question.problem:
Marcus has two spinners. The first of them has three sections labeled $1,2,3,$ and the second has four sections labeled $0,2,4,8.$ The random variable $X$ represents the number obtained on a typical throw of the first spinner, and $Y$ is the number obtained on a typical throw of the second spinner. The first spinner is rolled $10$ times, and the second spinner is rolled $5$ times. What is the expected value of the sum of all outcomes?
$x$ $1$ $2$ $3$
$f(x)$ $0.4$ $0.4$ $0.2$
$y$ $0$ $2$ $4$ $8$
$f(y)$ $0.5$ $0.3$ $0.1$ $0.1$
question.worked_solution:
Let ${X}_{i}$ be the $i$th score obtained from the first spinner, and let ${Y}_{j}$ be the $j$th score obtained from the second spinner. Then, we need to calculate 

$$
\text{E}[{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{X}_{i}+{\sum }_{j=1}^{5}{Y}_{j}].
$$

Using the properties of expected value, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{X}_{i}+{\sum }_{j=1}^{5}{Y}_{j}] & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{10}\text{E}[{X}_{i}]+{\sum }_{j=1}^{5}\text{E}[{Y}_{j}] \\  & =10\text{E}[X]+5\text{E}[Y],\end{aligned}
$$

where the last equality above is true because $\text{E}[{X}_{i}]=\text{E}[X]$ and $\text{E}[{Y}_{j}]=\text{E}[Y]$ for all $1\le i\le 10,\,1\le j\le 5.$

The expected values of $X$ and $Y$ are calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =1\cdot 0.4+2\cdot 0.4+3\cdot 0.2=1.8 \\ \text{E}[Y] & =0\cdot 0.5+2\cdot 0.3+4\cdot 0.1+8\cdot 0.1=1.8\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we get

$$
\text{E}[10X+5Y]=10\text{E}[X]+5\text{E}[Y]=10\cdot 1.8+5\cdot 1.8=27.
$$
